items.title: Chemours Shares Rise 6% After $455 Million North Carolina PFAS Settlement
items.summary: Chemours (NYSE:CC) shares rose 6% on Thursday after the company announced a settlement with the State of North Carolina and 11 local entities covering PFAS-related claims. The agreement resolves litigation concerning PFAS and other historical discharges from the Fayetteville Works facility, as well as claims involving alleged PFAS contamination unrelated to the site, including the use of aqueous film forming foam.

items.title: Chemours, DuPont and Corteva to Pay $455 Million in North Carolina PFAS Settlement
items.summary: The companies settled with North Carolina and 11 communities that were excluded from a previous settlement over drinking-water toxins.

items.summary: Corteva Chief Executive Chuck Magro says the company’s soon-to-be spun-off seed business, Vylor, could expand beyond corn and soybeans and into fruits and vegetables, aided by gene-editing advancements.

items.title: Corteva Says Farmers Are Willing to Pay Up for High-Tech Seeds
items.summary: Since the advent of Roundup Ready crops designed to withstand potent weedkillers, seeds and sprays have been entwined in the agriculture industry. Chuck Magro, CEO of Corteva, wants to undo that: Next month, his $55 billion company will split, creating separate businesses focusing on seeds and pesticides.
